recognize_zh: 低倍骨髓抹片中骨髓顆粒（particle）以脂肪空泡與基質為主，造血細胞稀少、只沿基質散在，並有深色染劑沉積，顯示骨髓細胞量偏低，可配合 Shwachman-Diamond 症候群的骨髓低細胞性；影像品質有限，無法評估細胞細節。
features: Low-power view of a marrow particle dominated by fat spaces and stromal strands
Sparse hematopoietic cells distributed along the stroma
Dark brown-black precipitate/pigment deposits and thick, poorly spread areas
Peripheral blood RBC background between particles
Magnification and preparation quality preclude assessment of individual cell morphology
describe_en: Low-power view of a bone marrow aspirate smear shows a particle composed predominantly of fat spaces and stromal elements with only sparse hematopoietic cells along its strands. Thick, dark areas with brown-black precipitate are present, and blood-diluted areas surround the particle. Cytologic detail, maturation, and dysplasia cannot be evaluated at this magnification. The overall impression is of a hypocellular particle, which in context is compatible with the marrow hypoplasia seen in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome; a core biopsy is needed for accurate cellularity assessment.

ddx.vs: Aplastic anemia also shows fatty hypocellular particles, but lacks pancreatic insufficiency, skeletal dysplasia, and biallelic SBDS mutations.
A hemodilute sample has few or no particles and many blood elements, whereas true hypocellularity shows fat-predominant particles; biopsy settles cellularity.
Hypocellular MDS shows dysplasia in residual cells, increased blasts, or clonal cytogenetics (e.g., monosomy 7), which must be evaluated at higher power.
